BiblicalUsage: gᵉdêrâh — wall, hedge. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 11 occurrences, and in Numbers, 1 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, and Psalms the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What gᵉdêrâh tells me is that God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: Reuben and Gad Settle East of the Jordan; David Spares Saul at En Gedi
